clue.text: A lot of grind — that could be positive or negative

parts.note: to mill is to grind, as corn in a mill

parts.words: that could be positive or negative
parts.note: an ion is a charged particle, carrying either a positive or a negative charge

explanation.surface: A long, dull stretch of work that might turn out well or badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A million is a very large number, so it stands for a huge quantity, as in 'a million things to do'.

clue.text: In which Liz Truss has delivered?

definitions.text: In which Liz Truss has delivered?

parts.words: In which Liz Truss has delivered?
parts.note: the former Prime Minister was known for flat, unvaried delivery of her speeches

explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' suggests a policy or a baby, but it is about speaking: Truss's speeches were often mocked for their flat, single-pitch voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A monotone is a voice that stays on one unvarying pitch, the manner of a dull speaker.

clue.text: Footwear is carbon free, for the record

indicators.note: free here means free of, without, so the carbon symbol is dropped

parts.note: a clog is a wooden shoe
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A claim that some shoes are made without any carbon emissions, stated on the record.
explanation.definitionFit: A log is a written record, such as a ship's log of its voyage.

clue.text: You're right, physio helped my posture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a phrase admitting a mistake
second meaning, taken literally: my standing has been corrected by treatment

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the phrase says that the way the speaker stands has been put right, which a physiotherapist might do.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'I stand corrected' concedes that someone else's point is accurate and your own was wrong.

clue.text: Upcoming police department has one rule that might be basic

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means read from bottom to top, so the pieces run in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
I is the Roman numeral for one
a canon is a rule or law

explanation.surface: A forthcoming police unit adopts a rule that could be rather elementary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'basic' looks like simple, but in chemistry a base is the opposite of an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that is not acidic may well be alkaline, which chemists call basic.

clue.text: Killer regularly stabbing workers in chains

indicators.note: the picked letters pierce into the middle of the other word, as a blade stabs into a body

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word Killer, starting with the first

parts.note: its odd letters are K, L, E

explanation.surface: A murderer attacks labourers who are bound in chains, like a chain gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Anklets are ornamental bands or fetters worn round the ankle, so a set of them can be chains.

clue.text: Mountain's not half hard for a Greek

parts.note: an alp is a mountain; the 's is 'has'

indicators.note: not half means without half its letters, so only the first half of hard remains

parts.note: its first half is HA

explanation.surface: A climb proves only moderately tough for a man from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek' looks like a person, but it means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a Greek character.

clue.text: Reason for facelift? Smiles, despite it all having gone wrong

definitions.meaning: first meaning, taken literally: a facelift holds up the jaw and chin

definitions.text: Smiles, despite it all having gone wrong
definitions.meaning: second meaning: stays cheerful in adversity

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical literal reading of the idiom; the second is its everyday meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep one's chin up is an idiom for staying cheerful and brave when things are going badly.

clue.text: After English pass, on to enter quality school

indicators.note: the rest of the answer comes after the English letter
the pass and on letters go inside the quality word, entering it

parts.note: tone is a quality, as of sound or colour
a col is a mountain pass
the on side in cricket is the leg side

explanation.surface: After passing English, a pupil moves on to an elite school.
explanation.walkthrough: COLLEG goes inside TONE, after E. Eton College is a famous English boys' public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a fee-paying boarding school near Windsor, one of England's best-known schools.

clue.text: Demonstrations of three elements

parts.note: the protests can be spelt out from chemical symbols: silicon, the metal tin, and sulphur

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits into SI (silicon), TIN and S (sulphur), three elements, while the whole is a kind of protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest in which people occupy a place and refuse to leave, a form of demonstration.

clue.text: This could precede cap and gown happening at the end of the day

definitions.text: This could precede cap and gown
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the word that goes before 'cap' and 'gown' to make nightcap and nightgown

definitions.text: happening at the end of the day
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the time that comes when the day is over

explanation.surface: Cap and gown suggest a graduation ceremony held late in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is the dark period that follows the end of the day, and it forms compounds such as nightcap and nightgown.

clue.text: Left province to sulk about exercise day

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province

indicators.note: the sulking word goes around the other letters, as something placed about them

parts.note: to pout is to sulk
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned a province in a huff over a day of exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a political or directional word, but here it is the past tense of leaving. Northern Ireland is often called simply the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: To have nipped out is to have left briefly and quickly, an informal phrase for popping out.

clue.text: Antics involved gagging angry niche experts

indicators.note: a gag goes over the mouth, so the outer letters hold the others inside them
involved means convoluted or tangled, so the letters of Antics are mixed up

parts.note: used as written

indicators.note: angry letters are worked up and disordered, so niche is rearranged

parts.note: used as written

explanation.surface: Pranks that involve silencing furious specialists in their own small field.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are rearranged separately: the scrambled niche sits inside the scrambled Antics, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Technicians are skilled specialists in a practical field, so they are experts in their trade.

clue.text: Enter tube gnashing teeth with caries

indicators.note: gnashing teeth grind together, so their letters and those of caries are ground into a new order

parts.note: used as written

explanation.surface: A dental scene: a tube is inserted while the patient grinds rotten teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To catheterise is to insert a catheter, a thin tube put into the body to drain fluid.

clue.text: Country wanting a Dutch amateur is the place to go

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so these letters are missing from the country

parts.note: Canada is a country

explanation.surface: A country lacking a Dutch amateur sportsman is the place to head for.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, D and A from CANADA. 'The can' is American slang for the toilet, the place you go when nature calls.
explanation.definitionFit: Can is slang for the lavatory, the room people euphemistically call the place to go.

clue.text: Saw new books on the shelf

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible
something iced is put on hold, shelved, just as a plan put on the shelf is deferred

explanation.surface: Someone spotted recently published books on display in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: To have noticed something is to have seen or observed it, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Stop the French mismanagement

parts.note: a bung is a stopper for a barrel or hole
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A call to halt French administrative failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungle is a clumsy mistake, so bad handling of affairs is a fair noun equivalent.

clue.text: Perhaps Tory U-turn after mistake is an accident waiting to happen

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the mistake in the answer

parts.note: a boob is a blunder

indicators.note: a U-turn turns the word back the other way

parts.note: the Tories are an example of a party

explanation.surface: A government blunder followed by a policy reversal is a disaster in the making.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative Party, so 'Perhaps' marks them as one example of a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby trap is a hidden device set to go off when disturbed, so harm lies in wait for whoever triggers it.

clue.text: Twist again, as Checker might

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to strain a muscle is to twist or wrench it

explanation.surface: Chubby Checker, singer of 'Let's Twist Again', is asked to repeat his dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Checker evokes the singer of 'Let's Twist Again', but a checker is anyone who checks, which is what restraining does.
explanation.definitionFit: A checker holds something back, and to restrain is to hold back or check.

clue.text: Some trickle-down reveals basis for assessment

indicators.note: the clue words reveal a word sitting inside them, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Trickle-down economics is shown to be the yardstick by which policy is judged.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across soME TRICkle.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric is a standard of measurement, the yardstick used when judging performance.

clue.text: Dirty smell set back prospect

indicators.note: set back means put in reverse, so the smell's letters run the other way

parts.note: BO is body odour, a bad smell
a prospect is a view or scene

explanation.surface: A foul smell spoils the outlook for a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material is indecent or smutty, which is what dirty jokes or books are.

clue.text: Our rivals with old blood-feud, primarily

definitions.text: Our rivals with old blood-feud, primarily

parts.note: them, as in us and them, are the other side

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of blood-feud is taken

explanation.surface: A gang talking about the rival outfit with whom they have a long vendetta.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the Mafia, known for rivalries and blood feuds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mob is the Mafia, an organised crime family that fights long, violent vendettas with rival gangs.

clue.text: Shouting takes place now and again in the UAE

indicators.note: now and again means at intervals, so only every other letter of the UAE is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of these words are taken, skipping the rest

explanation.surface: Occasional shouting goes on in the United Arab Emirates.
explanation.walkthrough: The UAE is the United Arab Emirates. Hue survives mainly in the phrase 'hue and cry', a loud public outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hue is an old word for outcry or clamour, as in hue and cry, the noise raised to pursue a criminal.

clue.text: Vacuous personnel piercing nipple? That just won't happen

parts.note: vacuous means empty

indicators.note: the personnel letters go through the nipple word, as a stud pierces it

parts.note: a teat is a nipple
HR is human resources, the personnel department

explanation.surface: An airhead from the staff gets a nipple piercing.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty threat is a warning with no intention of being carried out, so the menace never comes.

clue.text: Nick just a little bit

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a tiny amount, as of salt

explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for steal, and also a noun for a cut; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinch is informal for stealing, and a pinch is the small amount held between finger and thumb.

clue.text: Met Rose in shower to get wetter

indicators.note: a shower scatters things all over, so the letters are sprayed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone met Rose under the shower and got soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' reads as the bathroom fixture, but it is the anagram signal; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A moistener is something that dampens, so it is literally a thing that makes things wet.

clue.text: South African native is overwhelmed by any alarm

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped by, so the answer is buried inside the words any alarm

explanation.surface: A South African is panicked by every alarm that sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'native' sounds like a person, but the nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa, found inside aNY ALArm.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is an antelope that lives wild in southern Africa, so it is an animal native to that region.

clue.text: Love promotion to start commotion

indicators.note: the promotion piece is placed at the beginning, ahead of the love letter

parts.note: an ad promotes a product
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Romance gets a push and kicks up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bustle, as in much ado about nothing, a synonym for commotion.

clue.text: Scope the bard out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or off, so the letters of the bard are put in a different order

explanation.surface: An instruction to check out Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadth means range or extent, as in the breadth of a subject, which is its scope.

clue.text: For Spooner, dubious material for policemen is something to chew on

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first letters of the two pieces change places

parts.note: a cop is a policeman, here used as a modifier
porn is morally dubious material

explanation.surface: Seedy reading matter for the police becomes a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: COP PORN with the first letters exchanged becomes POP CORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is a snack of puffed maize kernels, food that people munch at the cinema.
